演奏時通常以手或木棒撥動張緊的金屬弦，有時也用輔助弓擦弦；喀拉拉的 Onavil: Playing usually sets the taut metal string going with the hand or a wooden stick, and sometimes a second bow is used to scrape it; the Onavillu of Kerala is struck with a thin stick. The instrument has no resonator built in, so a beginner can first put one end in the mouth, or stand the bow on a pit in the ground or hang a gourd on it, to make the sound clear. The mouth cavity can be changed in size as you play, so that the overtones form a melody. The basic order of work: fix the bow, keep the string taut, pluck the open note, then stop the string with a finger to get the other fundamental; in Xhosa the open note is called vu (open) and the stopped note ba (held), and the interval between them is mostly a whole tone, though in Zulu or Tsonga it can be smaller. In Africa it is mostly played by a solo performer, while capoeira uses it within a circle formation.

起源與獵弓關係不確定；喀拉哈里沙漠桑人會將獵弓轉為音樂用途。有學者推測約西元前一: The relation of its origin to the hunting bow is uncertain; the San of the Kalahari do turn hunting bows to musical use. Some scholars suggest that cave images of about 13,000 BC may show a musical bow being played, but the reading is disputed. Sachs held that the oldest musical bows were too long and had no place in hunters' rites, so he did not treat them as hunting bows; he still saw them as a key step in the development of chordophones: from the single-string bow that needs a resonator came one note per string, then added strings and the bow harp, harp and lyre, and then the straightening of the bow and the addition of a bridge produced the lute. Later, through cultural exchange, it reached Brazil, the Appalachians, Guam, Mauritius, Réunion, New Zealand, Hawaii and Curaçao.

非洲弓豎琴常見於獨奏場合，也見於卡波耶拉音樂團體「羅達」，其中 berimbau: The musical bow is mostly found as a solo instrument, and also in the roda, the circle of capoeira musicians, where the berimbau and the dancers and players at the centre of the circle make up the performance. The Appalachian mouth-bow can be played amplified in old-time music jams. The Tepehuán people of Mexico use a musical bow with a gourd resonator in their mitote ceremony; on the island of Curaçao the benta serves as the leading instrument of 'ghost music'.
非洲弓豎琴為弦鳴樂器，H-S 311.1，屬棒狀齊特琴類。構造通常是一根具彈性的: The musical bow is a chordophone, H-S 311.1, belonging to the bar zithers. It is usually a flexible wooden stick about 0.5 to 3 m long, strung end to end with a taut metal string; it is plucked with the hand or a wooden stick, and can also be bowed with a second bow. The sound usually relies on a resonator, such as a gourd, a pit in the ground or the player's mouth. It is used by African peoples and by Indigenous peoples of the Americas; in Africa it is mostly played by a solo performer, and it also appears in the capoeira circle of Brazil, in Appalachian old-time music gatherings, and in Mexico.

非洲弓豎琴的琴身多為具彈性的木條，長度約0.5至3公尺，兩端以緊繃弦線相連，弦線: The body of the musical bow is mostly a flexible wooden stick about 0.5 to 3 m long, with a taut string, usually of metal, joining the two ends. It can be plucked, bowed or struck with the hand or a wooden stick. The resonator is often a gourd attached to the back of the string bearer; one end may be put into the mouth, or a pit in the ground or a gourd used to resonate. Other regions use copper strings, bamboo bodies, gut, coconut shell, matai wood and fibre strings; where the sources do not say, nothing is assumed.
非洲弓豎琴音色溫潤而富有穿透力，具有獨特的親密感與靈性。其音域跨越中高音區，音色: The musical bow's timbre is warm and carries well, with an unusual intimacy and something of the spirit. Its range crosses the upper middle register, the sound both bright and dark, and each string brings subtle changes of overtone. The resonance chamber of the body is small, so the volume is relatively restrained yet full of layers. Next to the classical harp the musical bow sounds rougher and plainer, and you can still hear the finger's touch on the string; next to the guitar it is softer and warmer, without the guitar's crisp edge. The string and the body resonate directly, which gives it a particular organic feel, and its sound has a meditative, healing quality; it is widely used in world music and ambient composition.
